text:
alyssa: Hey team — noticed two engineers got tenant-admin rights out of nowhere this morning during routine access review. Not from manual grant, looks like provisioning noise. Can someone check SCIM logs? :eyes:
marco: On it. Which users?
alyssa: `sam.p` and `maya.k`. Audit shows role change at 2026-03-20T08:12:03Z from service account `okta-sync-sa`.
kevin: I pulled the provisioning log, there's a spike of group-updates around that time. Lots of nested-group apply ops.
jess: Pasting the relevant snippet from okta-sync logs:
```
2026-03-20T08:11:58Z INFO apply_group_update groupId=G-482 nested_groups=[G-211, G-482]
2026-03-20T08:12:03Z INFO assign_role user=sam.p role=tenant-admin source=group:G-482
2026-03-20T08:12:04Z INFO assign_role user=maya.k role=tenant-admin source=group:G-482
```
marco: Wait `nested_groups=[G-211, G-482]` — group pointing to itself. Looks like a circular nesting.
okta-sync-bot: Detected circular group reference: G-482 -> G-211 -> G-482 (count=3). Auto-retry suppressed.
alyssa: That explains the permission duplication. But why did the sync assign admin role instead of skipping? We have rule: group G-482 -> role tenant-admin. It shouldn't be applied repeatedly.
kevin: Current provisoner does naive DFS; when it revisits a group it still applies membership diffs which triggers idempotent assign_role code that mistakenly logs repeated grants and our audit interprets them as distinct. Root cause = circular group reference + lack of visited-set in sync.
jess: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) Pause SCIM provisioning via Okta pause endpoint, 2) Revoke tenant-admin from affected accounts, 3) Rotate `okta-sync-sa` API key (KMS in keys/secrets), 4) Open an incident ticket and set severity P2.
devops: I've paused the provisioning job (okta -> provisioning -> paused) and created a KMS rotation task for `okta-sync-sa` key. Ticket INC-2026-042 created.
sre-oncall: Revoke executed: removed tenant-admin from sam.p and maya.k at 08:27Z. Confirmed no active admin sessions.
kevin: I'll push a hotfix to the provisioner to add a visited-set and prevent re-entrant application of the same group. Small change, tests included. PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/provisioner/pulls/812
marco: Also recommend adding a validation in the console: detect circular group refs on import and reject with a clear error to the IdP owner.
security-bot: Flagging for postmortem. Please attach exports: provisioning logs, Okta group definitions, and the exact SCIM payloads.
alyssa: Yep adding to INC-2026-042. Also let's add an audit log tag when auto-fallback/retry happens so we don't confuse duplicates with new grants.
jess: One more note — double-check KMS audit for any access by `okta-sync-sa` around time window. If we rotate keys we need to update the deploy in staging/dedicated.
devops: Rotated key and updated secret in k8s `provisioner-okta` secret across env: staging and prod. Will monitor for errors.
kevin: Hotfix merged to main and deployed to prod with a canary. Monitor dashboards for group-change error rate.
marco: Postmortem TODOs: root cause writeup, add visited-set, console validation, add unit test for circular groups, add SCIM payload dedupe, KMS rotation runbook.
alyssa: Thanks all. Nice catch by the audit review. Assigning owners: kevin (fix), jess (incident lead), devops (key rotation), marco (postmortem). Will follow up in INC-2026-042. :thumbsup:
